module_title: Union Executive: President, VP, and PM - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India. It is dealt with in Part V of the Constitution (Articles 52 to 78). In India, we have a parliamentary form of government where the President is the nominal head and the PM is the real head.

core_concepts.title: The President (Article 52)
core_concepts.description: The President is the 'Head of the State' and the first citizen of India. He acts as the symbol of unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation. Though all executive actions are taken in his name, he is a nominal executive (De Jure head).

core_concepts.title: The Vice-President (Article 63)
core_concepts.description: The Vice-President holds the second-highest office in the country. His main role is to act as the Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. If the President's office falls vacant, he acts as the President for a maximum of six months.

core_concepts.title: The Prime Minister (Article 75)
core_concepts.description: The Prime Minister is the 'Head of the Government' and the real executive (De Facto head). He is appointed by the President, usually being the leader of the party with a majority in the Lok Sabha.

core_concepts.title: Qualifications for President & VP
core_concepts.description: To be elected, a person must: 1. Be a citizen of India. 2. Be at least 35 years of age. 3. For President: Be qualified for election as a member of Lok Sabha. 4. For VP: Be qualified for election as a member of Rajya Sabha.

important_entities.name: The Electoral College
important_entities.significance: Includes elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.

important_entities.name: Council of Ministers
important_entities.significance: They aid and advise the President in the exercise of his functions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Nominated members of Parliament do NOT participate in the election of the President, but they DO participate in the election of the Vice-President.
Do not confuse the two: President = Nominal/Head of State; PM = Real/Head of Government.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The President, Vice-President, and Governors all require a minimum age of 35 years.

exam_strategy_tips: Remember that the President is elected indirectly, not directly by the people.
The Vice-President's salary is paid to him in his capacity as the Chairman of Rajya Sabha, not as the VP.
